system: You are a senior Blender technical artist. You write complete, runnable Blender Python (bpy) scripts for headless rendering. Reply with ONE python code block only, no commentary.
prompt:
Write a complete Blender 5.2 Python (bpy) script that builds and renders the following animated shot entirely procedurally, for headless use: `Blender -b --factory-startup -P book_open.py --python-exit-code 1`.

SHOT: "book_open" for Nightlight Press, a children's picture-book publisher. 200 frames at 30 fps (frames 1..200, about 6.7 s), 1600x900.
Style: warm, sunny, rounded clay / paper-cut miniature diorama (think stop-motion storybook set). Soft matte materials, rounded bevelled edges everywhere, gentle saturated colors, nothing photoreal-gritty.
Palette (sRGB hex; convert to linear before assigning to Base Color): paper FFF8EC, ink 22223B, tomato FF6B4A, sun FFC233, sky 4DA8DA, leaf 3BB273, lilac B8A1FF. Wood tones: warm honey browns (e.g. C98A55, B5743F, D9A066).

SCENE CONTENT
1. A sunlit wooden table: a few long rounded planks (bevelled boxes) in slightly different honey wood tones, large enough to fill the frame below the book. Behind it, a soft warm cream backdrop (curved or a large plane) far enough back to go out of focus. Add 2-3 simple out-of-focus props in the background on the table (e.g. a sky-blue clay mug = cylinder, a little leaf-green clay plant = a few spheres on a short cylinder pot, a lilac ball) to give miniature depth and bokeh.
2. A hardcover picture book lying flat on the table, landscape format, about W=2.0 (x) by D=1.5 (y). Spine along the line x=0 (book occupies x in [0, 2.0] when closed). Construction:
   - back board (tomato, ~0.04 thick, bevelled) at the bottom, under the right half;
   - lower half page block (paper color, slightly inset from the boards) on the back board;
   - a "front half" unit = front cover board (tomato, bevelled) + upper half page block, sitting on top;
   - on the front cover centre: a small raised sun emblem (sun-yellow disc plus 8-10 small rounded rays, slightly emissive so it glows a bit) and a thin paper-colored title strip under it. Parent these to the cover.
   - a rounded tomato spine piece at x=0.
   OPENING (the book opens at its middle): the front-half unit rotates 180 degrees about a hinge line at the spine (x=0, parallel to y) located at the book's mid-height, so it lands flat on the table to the LEFT (cover face down, upper page block now on top on the left). Use an Empty as the hinge pivot and keyframe its Y rotation. Timing: frames 20 -> 70 with ease-in/ease-out, plus a tiny overshoot/settle.
3. PAGES FAN OPEN ONE AFTER ANOTHER: 6 thin individual pages (paper color, ~0.006 thick, subdivided along x) lie stacked on top of the right (lower) page block. Each has its own hinge Empty at the spine at its own height. Starting at frame 62, every ~11 frames the next page lifts and flips right -> left over ~30 frames (ease in/out), ending a few degrees short of 180 (e.g. 176, 173, 170, 167, 164, 161 degrees) so the flipped pages fan slightly above the left side instead of intersecting. Give each flipping page a gentle paper curl while moving: a Simple Deform modifier (BEND) whose angle is keyframed 0 -> about 35-45 degrees mid-flip -> 0 at rest (use a deform-axis / origin setup that works; if it is not robust, skip the curl rather than break the script). Small z-gaps everywhere to avoid z-fighting.
4. THE REVEALED SPREAD: on the top surface of the right page block (revealed after the last page flips) and on the back of the last flipped page, place a simple paper-cut illustration made of thin raised flat shapes: rolling leaf-green hills (flattened scaled cylinders / spheres clipped by the page), a sun-yellow sun disc, a sky-blue cloud made of 3 merged flat discs, a lilac little moon or star, and a tiny tomato house (box + wedge roof). Keep them thin (0.01) so they read as paper cut-outs.
5. MAGIC LIGHT: a warm golden point light hovering just above the gutter (x=0, centre of the spread) whose power ramps from 0 (before frame 60) up to strong by frame ~120, with a gentle flicker/pulse after; plus a soft emissive golden glow disc/plane just above the gutter that fades in (keep it subtle, it should feel like light coming out of the pages).
6. SPARKLES AND PAPER STARS rising out of the pages: ~80 small emissive UV spheres (radius 0.012-0.03, low segment count, emission colors: mostly warm white/sun yellow, a few lilac and tomato, emission strength high enough to bloom, e.g. 6-20) and ~16 small five-pointed paper stars (build the star mesh with bmesh or from_pydata: 10-vertex outline, extruded ~0.012, sun-yellow and paper colors, mildly emissive ~1-3). They spawn between frames 75 and 185 (staggered, random but seeded: random.seed(7)) from random points over the open spread near the gutter, rise 0.8-2.0 units upward while drifting sideways along a gentle sinusoid (keyframe location every ~8 frames), stars also spin slowly. Each one scales 0 -> 1 when born and back to 0 near the end of its life (life 50-90 frames). Hide everything before birth with scale 0 (do NOT use particle systems).
7. CAMERA: 50 mm lens, 3/4 high angle looking down at the book from the front (negative y side) and slightly right, with a Track To constraint on a target Empty. Framing: at frame 1 the closed book sits in the middle of the frame with plenty of table around; over the full 200 frames the camera does a slow smooth push-in (about 25-30% closer) and the target Empty glides from the closed-book centre (x~1.0, z~0.2) to the open-spread centre (x~0, z~0.3), so that at the end the open spread (about 4.1 x 1.5 units) fills about 70% of the frame width and the rising sparkles are visible above it. Depth of field: camera.data.dof.use_dof = True, focus_object = target Empty, aperture_fstop around 2.0-2.8 so the background props are softly blurred but the whole book stays sharp.

LIGHTING
- A warm sun light (color ~FFE6BF, strength 3-4, angle ~0.15 rad for soft shadows) from upper left and slightly behind, giving warm long-ish soft shadows on the table.
- A large soft warm area light as key from front-right above, plus a weaker cool-ish fill area light (very slightly sky-tinted) from the left.
- World background: soft warm cream color at low strength for ambient.

RENDER / TECHNICAL CONSTRAINTS (important)
- Blender 5.2 bpy. Start by clearing the default scene (delete all objects, or build in a fresh scene).
- Engine: scene.render.engine = 'BLENDER_EEVEE' (wrap in try/except; if that enum fails try 'BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT'). EEVEE render samples via scene.eevee.taa_render_samples.
- Build everything procedurally from primitives / bmesh (no external files, no add-ons, no image textures). Use Bevel modifiers (or subdivision) for soft clay/paper rounded edges.
- Materials: simple Principled BSDF only (roughness ~0.6-0.9, maybe a little Sheen/Coat for clay), Principled input names in Blender 4.x/5.x are 'Base Color', 'Roughness', 'Emission Color', 'Emission Strength', 'Sheen Weight', 'Coat Weight', 'Subsurface Weight'. Set them defensively (skip a missing input instead of crashing).
- Bloom: EEVEE's old bloom toggle no longer exists. Use the compositor Glare node with glare_type 'BLOOM' (fallback 'FOG_GLOW'), moderate threshold/size/mix so emissive sparkles, the sun emblem and the golden glow bloom softly. NOTE: in Blender 5.x the compositor is no longer scene.node_tree with a Composite node: create a node group with bpy.data.node_groups.new('Comp', 'CompositorNodeTree'), assign it to scene.compositing_node_group, add a 'NodeGroupOutput' node and create its output socket via tree.interface.new_socket(name='Image', in_out='OUTPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketColor'); Render Layers -> Glare -> Group Output. Some Glare settings in 5.x are input sockets rather than node properties (e.g. 'Type', 'Quality', 'Threshold', 'Size', 'Strength' style inputs) - set each setting defensively: if node.inputs has a matching socket set its default_value, else set the attribute if it exists. Make sure scene.render.use_compositing is True. Wrap the whole compositor setup in try/except so a compositor API mismatch only prints a warning and the render still happens.
- Depth of field via camera.data.dof.
- Sparkles/dust are small emissive spheres animated with keyframes (no particle systems). Keep total object count reasonable (<300).
- Lights: one sun light + area lights (+ the golden point light).
- Color management: view_transform 'AgX' (fallback 'Filmic', then 'Standard'), exposure ~0, keep the image bright, warm and sunny (not dark, not grey).
- Output: PNG RGB 8-bit frames. Read these environment variables (with defaults):
    OUTPUT_DIR (required; create it if missing) - frames written as OUTPUT_DIR/frame_####.png
    RES_X (default 1600), RES_Y (default 900), resolution_percentage 100
    SAMPLES (default 24) - EEVEE render samples
    FRAME_LIST (optional, comma separated frame numbers, e.g. "1,60,120,180"): if set, render only those frames as stills (scene.frame_set(f); render.filepath = OUTPUT_DIR/frame_%04d.png; bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)); otherwise render the full animation frames 1..200 with bpy.ops.render.render(animation=True) and render.filepath = OUTPUT_DIR/frame_ .
  scene.render.fps = 30, frame_start = 1, frame_end = 200. Motion blur off. Keep render time small.
- All keyframes should use smooth easing (Bezier); for repeating drift you may set keyframes densely. Use keyframe_insert(data_path=..., frame=...). Do not use fcurve.keyframe_points.insert on Blender 5 actions (the layered Action API changed); if you need to adjust interpolation, do it defensively with try/except.
- Print a short progress line per rendered frame and a final "DONE" line.
Reply with the full script in a single python code block.
feedback_prompt:
Art-director review of the full 1600x900 render of the script above (it renders cleanly in Blender 5.2.1, no errors, no z-fighting, camera move is smooth, sparkles and bloom read well). This is the final polish pass for a stage screen / projector, so contrast and color matter. Keep EVERYTHING that works: same env-var interface (OUTPUT_DIR, RES_X, RES_Y, SAMPLES, FRAME_LIST), same frame_####.png output naming, same 200-frame timing, same book construction and opening, same camera path and DOF, same sparkles/stars/gutter glow. Change only the following:

1. WASHED-OUT PEACH HAZE (most important). Every frame sits under a pale peach veil: mean luma is ~185/255 and average saturation is low, so on a projector it will look foggy. Likely causes: the Glare node (threshold 1.0) is blooming the paper pages and lit wood, the paper has self-emission, and the world fill is strong. Fix:
   - Glare: raise threshold to about 1.8-2.2 so ONLY the emissive sparkles, paper stars, sun emblem and gutter glow exceed it; keep strength/size moderate; the glare must only ADD light around those emitters, never lift the whole frame.
   - Paper self-emission: 0 (the paper should read cream from lighting alone). Keep the sparkles/stars/glow emission values as they are (raise sparkle emission a little if needed so they still bloom with the higher threshold).
   - World strength about 0.25-0.3; fill light a bit weaker so there are real soft shadows under the book, the lifted pages and the props.
   - Color management: AgX with look 'AgX - Punchy' (fallback 'AgX - Medium High Contrast'), exposure about 0.0-0.1. Target: mean luma ~150-165/255, clearly visible soft shadows, whites of the pages still bright cream (not grey), overall still warm, sunny and cheerful - not dark.
2. COVER COLOR: the cover, back board and spine read as pale salmon/pink, not tomato. They must read as a saturated tomato red-orange (target on screen close to FF6B4A). Use a slightly deeper/more saturated base color for the boards (e.g. hex F2552F) and keep their roughness ~0.6 so highlights don't wash them out. Same for the tiny tomato houses.
3. BLANK PAGES FOR TWO THIRDS OF THE CLIP: from frame ~60 to ~130 the audience sees only blank white pages; the illustration only appears when the last leaf lands. Make the page turn colorful:
   - Put a simple paper-cut illustration on BOTH faces of every one of the 6 turning leaves, each different, reusing the existing illustration builder with variations from the palette, e.g.: a night page (ink 22223B rectangle panel with a lilac moon and sun-yellow stars), a sea page (sky-blue wavy band with a tomato sail boat), a meadow with a big leaf-green round tree, a sunny field with a big sun-yellow sun and rays, a lilac hill with a tomato balloon, a sky page with clouds and a kite. Keep shapes big and bold (readable at 1600x900), thin (~0.008-0.01) and slightly raised.
   - The top face of the right page block that is revealed at the end and the back of the last leaf should form ONE panoramic final spread (hills continuing across the gutter, sun on the left page, house + cloud on the right page) instead of the same picture repeated on both sides.
   - CUT-OUTS MUST STAY GLUED TO THEIR LEAF: in the current render, around frames 135-145, the sun disc on the turning last leaf floats in the air off the page. Make each leaf's cut-outs deform with it robustly: join the cut-out meshes into the leaf mesh (bmesh / object join) BEFORE adding the curl shape key, with enough subdivision in the cut-outs that they bend with the paper. Keep the small z offsets so nothing z-fights.
4. FRAMING POLISH: at the very end the plant is cut by the right frame edge and the mug by the top edge. Move the plant a little left/back and the mug a little down so both remain mostly in frame (still soft-focus) during frames 150-200. Keep the push-in and DOF.
5. Keep object count under ~300 and render time small (no new lights beyond what exists; no particle systems).

Reply with the complete revised script in a single python code block.
